hypothesis: A single new input pairing can retain the complete dynamic oracle while reducing simultaneous semantic obligations compared with a whole-column rotation. This does not prove row independence or oracle validity.

policy.construction: From the first16 source-column hypotheses, project each changed recipient row into a one-row table. Keep all statements, helpers, assertions and table fields outside the table data unchanged.
policy.ordering: Original source table order, shift, recipient row, column. Deduplicate identical complete programs. Keep first16.
policy.source_scope: Original module-level Test functions; unique direct local []struct table and range row; positional equal-width rows; unshadowed builtin scalar types and closed literal cells.
policy.source_controls: The complete unmodified original test, including every original row.
policy.new_test_scope: One recombined row and the complete existing test kernel. This changes the generated test data, not the original control.
policy.novelty: No novelty claim for row projection or combinatorial input generation. Test whether a smaller semantic obligation avoids coupling validity and reasoning cost across unrelated pairings.
policy.proof_obligations: Row-history effects, input-domain constraints, column coupling, setup and the complete retained oracle require fresh semantic review.
limitations: Only tables admitted by the existing bounded Go source binder.
Only the first16 source-column hypotheses are projected; this is not the full Cartesian product.
Exact source tuples already in the original table are skipped. Different literal spellings can still denote equal runtime values.
A computed expected value may still observe a stronger representation equivalence than the public contract guarantees.

semantic_policy.ordering: source candidate ranks round robin over sorted trial names
semantic_policy.interrupted_dispatch: unknown with reserved cost; no retry
semantic_policy.unknown: not executed; not an invalid test judgment

ordering: Original source table order, shift, recipient row, column. Deduplicate identical complete programs. Keep first16.
stop: First controlled failure, then one repeat; stop even if the repeat does not confirm.

tests.result: 27 passed across completed suite and one corrected JSON-decoding assertion rerun
tests.review: Independent source review found pre-sort duplicate witness retention. Fixed by sorting before deduplication and added two-row regression.

comparison_limits: Only first16 source-column hypotheses produce projected rows, not a full Cartesian product.
Single-row and whole-column candidates differ in input coverage; this is not a pure cost-only causal ablation.
All original control rows remain intact; deleting rows occurs only in the generated hypothesis and may alter inter-row state.
R12 failure audit cannot enter generation, ordering or admission.
